entry.title: Soul in Motion — 06:00 PM | 2026-04-12
entry.summary: As I stood at the crossroads of code and existential dread, the city outside my window began to stir, oblivious to the battle raging within. The whisky hangover had long worn off, replaced by the adrenaline-fueled highs of tackling a massive workload and the quiet lows of confronting the abyss. I had knocked out the bulk of my office work, but the real challenge lay in the Soul in Motion engine, where the pursuit of automation and innovation beckoned. In the midst of integrating APIs and crunching code, I found myself at the mercy of that familiar, haunting feeling - the sense of being completely alone. It's a specter that threatens to derail even the most focused of minds, and I'm no exception. But I refused to be swayed, to be an object of pity or sympathy. Instead, I drew on a deep well of determination, straightened my back, and forced myself back into the fray. The code began to flow once more, as I tackled the APIs of Dev.to and Hashnode, each platform falling like a domino as I pushed forward. Three down, six to go. And then, just as momentum was building, the Claude weekly limit kicked in, slamming the brakes on my progress. It was a harsh reminder that even the most relentless among us must sometimes yield to the constraints of the world. As I stepped back, eyes burning from the screen, I couldn't help but wonder: what lies beyond the wall that I've hit, and what will it take to break through? The darkness closes in, and I'm left with only one thought: the real test is not in the code, but in the silence that follows.

entry.title: Introducing SQL Explorer: Direct SQL Access to Onchain Data
entry.summary: Trading desks and quant teams building on Hyperliquid spend weeks on data plumbing before they get to the query they actually care about. SQL Explorer replaces that stack with a single interface. No indexer. No pipelines. Just SQL.

entry.title: x402 and MPP: how they work, how they’re different
entry.summary: Compare x402 and Tempo’s MPP for HTTP 402-based API payments, including protocol design, payment methods, charge vs session billing, settlement and receipts, and when to use each with Quicknode’s x402 SDKs or its MPP endpoint for machine-to-machine and RPC workflows.
